titel: Coyote vs. Acme with Dave Green, Phil Lord and Christopher Miller (Ep. 620)

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: Director Dave Green discusses making the hybrid comedy Coyote vs. Acme.
kurzfassung: Director Dave Green discusses the turbulent journey and creative process behind his hybrid film Coyote vs. Acme. In conversation with Phil Lord and Christopher Miller, he explains how his team brought animated characters to life on set alongside live actors. The discussion also covers the film's themes of resilience and the unexpected cultural resonance of the project.
stichpunkte: Dave Green directed Coyote vs. Acme, a hybrid comedy blending live-action and classic cartoon characters.
The production utilized a life-size puppet of Wile E. Coyote and a team of puppeteers to help actors interact with a non-existent co-star.
A lengthy story and previs process helped establish the visual language and comedic timing before shooting on location in Albuquerque.
The project drew inspiration from classic legal thrillers and courtroom dramas like Erin Brockovich and The Verdict.
Animators from diverse backgrounds, including traditional and contemporary cartoon styles, contributed to the film's fast-paced visual gags.
After facing shelving and an uncertain release status, the film gained widespread community support and advocacy from its cast and crew.

kapitel.titel: Bringing Wile E. Coyote to Set
Audience Ownership and Re-watching the Film
Animation Style and Termite Terrace Influences

clips.hook: A screening that generated universal praise before studio shelving.
clips.text: An early studio screening left every attendee enthusiastic about the picture, only for all subsequent viewings to be abruptly halted for three years.

clips.hook: A foam puppet standing in for an invisible co-star.
clips.text: A physical maquette with interchangeable facial expressions was operated on set to give performers a concrete eye-line and spatial reference.

clips.hook: A cartoon historian's surprising reason for classic short greatness.
clips.text: An animation expert attributed the exceptional quality of vintage studio shorts entirely to a lack of close supervision and pure neglect.

clips.hook: A stunt double swap noticed by an attentive viewer.
clips.text: An audience member publicly pointed out a classic cinematic switch where a stunt performer entered the water and an actor emerged.

clips.hook: Recognizing the collaborative writer's room on screen.
clips.text: The speakers note how the collective energy of artists sharing ideas in a single building is visibly embedded in the final product.

beschreibung:
Director Dave Green discuss his new film, Coyote vs. Acme, with fellow Directors Phil Lord and Christopher Miller in a Q&A at the DGA theater in Los Angeles. In the conversation, he discusses the story behind the film’s distribution, his on-set tactics for shooting a mixed live action/animation film, and working with animators from a variety of backgrounds to capture the energy of the Looney Tunes series.

The film tells the story of Wile E. Coyote, who, after decades of enduring catastrophic product failures at the hands of ACME Inc., decides to finally fight back. Teaming up with a billboard accident lawyer, he takes on the company and their slick corporate counsel, exposing a cover-up that’s been blowing him up in the name of profit.
